1:# British Fencing rankings as a standings source: a fourth scope on the existing response model, but not a second identity space in the standings index
2-
3-- **Status:** Design — implemented, with a later reversal of where the membership id lives (see [Decision reversal (2026-09-04)](#decision-reversal-2026-09-04)).
4-- **Date:** 2026-09-02
5-- **Amended:** 2026-09-04 — licence is a shared fencer property, not a per-account assertion.
6-- **Work item:** `Design British Fencing rankings as a standings source` (`exec_18d19ee554400638_43e`)
7-- **Parent project:** British Fencing rankings as a standings source
8-- **Sources verified:** both live-ranking tables fetched and fully parsed on 2026-09-02 (see [Source contract, measured](#source-contract-measured))
9-- **Related:** [Fencer standings callout on Results page](fencer-standings-callout-on-results-page.md) (the chip this extends), [Unified rankings ingest](unified-rankings-ingest-usa-fencing-s-new-unified-rankings.md) (the snapshot/last-known-good precedent), [Standings points composition](standings-points-composition-expose-what-contributes-to-a-tracked-fencer-s-standing.md) (the breakdown this extends), [Standings data freshness](standings-data-freshness-staleness-indicators-ingestion-error-handling.md) (not started)
10-
11-## TL;DR
12-
13-British Fencing's published live-ranking tables become a **fourth `scope` on the existing per-fencer standings contract** — alongside `national`, `regional`, and `unified` — reusing the existing chip, the existing breakdown modal, the existing background-task framework, and Redis. They do **not** enter `standings:index`, because that index's load-bearing property is that every row in it is addressed by a USA Fencing membership number, and a British licence is a different identity space.
14-
15-The contested part of that bet, and the thing a reviewer should push on: **the standings _response_ model is governing-body-agnostic and the standings _index_ is not.** Someone could reasonably argue for uniformity — put British rows in `standings:index` too. The [Chosen approach](#chosen-approach) argues why that trades a real invariant for a cosmetic one.
16-
17-Everything the breakdown needs is published. The tables carry a per-event **placing and points** pair plus per-fencer **domestic and international subtotals with counts**, and from those the exact counted set reconstructs and reconciles against the published total on **101 of 101 rows** across both tables — so British can honour the same reconcile-or-refuse contract every other composition source already honours.
18-
19:## Goals
20-
21-1. **Ingest both published tables** — Cadet Women's Sabre and Junior Women's Sabre — on a daily schedule matching the source's own publish cadence, storing rank, name, year of birth, club, licence, total, the domestic/international split, and every per-event column with its event name, date, placing, and points.
22-2. **A British Fencing membership id on the fencer**, editable by anyone who tracks them, joined to each table's `Licence` column. Optional; most fencers will never have one. Two accounts tracking the same fencer see the same value.
23-3. **A standings chip per table the fencer is ranked on**, on both the owner's Results page and its unauthenticated shared-results view, in the same visual family as the existing chips (`CDTWS #12 of 58 · 37,210 pts · British`), with a **British flag** icon where the existing chips show a trophy, globe, or pin.
24-4. **Clicking the chip opens a per-competition points breakdown** built from the table's own event columns: each event's name, date, placing, and points contributed, split into what counted and what did not, with the domestic/international subtotals.
25-5. **Not-yet-ranked is a first-class, silent state.** A configured licence that matches no row on a table produces no chip for that table — no error, no warning, no empty chip — and the chip appears on its own at the first daily refresh where the licence shows up.
26-6. **Adding a third table is configuration, not code.**
27-
28-## Non-goals
29-
30-- **Any other British Fencing data.** Results, events, calendar, club data — none of it. Rankings only.
31-- **Tables beyond the two named.** The mechanism generalises; the deployed set does not grow in this project.
32-- **iOS.** No iOS work is proposed. See [iOS needs no change, and why that is load-bearing](#ios-needs-no-change-and-why-that-is-load-bearing) — this is a decision the design made, not a topic it skipped.
33-- **Automatic discovery or name-matching of a fencer's licence.** A user types the number.
34-- **Using British rankings in recommendations, plan-page ratings, projected impact, or qualification.** The chip and its breakdown, nothing else. `crate::recommendations::standings` is an in-process consumer of the same fetch path and must be unaffected.
35-- **A British whole-list Standings page.** The Standings page keeps its three scopes.
36-- **Reproducing British Fencing's ranking policy.** Flunge reports what the source publishes. It does not model why an event counted.
37-
38-## Source contract, measured
39-
40-Everything below was fetched and parsed on 2026-09-02, not inferred. Both tables:
41-
42-| Property                | Cadet Women's Sabre                        | Junior Women's Sabre                        |
43-| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
44-| URL                     | `.../live-ranking/cadet-womens-sabre.html` | `.../live-ranking/junior-womens-sabre.html` |
45-| Body size               | 51,339 bytes                               | 40,265 bytes                                |
46-| `last-modified`         | `Tue, 01 Sep 2026 05:12:24 GMT`            | `Tue, 01 Sep 2026 05:12:14 GMT`             |
47-| In-table `Last update:` | `01/09/2026 04:30`                         | `01/09/2026 04:29`                          |
48-| Data rows               | **58**                                     | **43**                                      |
49-| Highest rank            | **48**                                     | **38**                                      |
50-| Event columns           | 16                                         | 16                                          |
51-
52-Structural facts, all confirmed against both files:
53-
54-- **Static server-rendered HTML.** One `<table>`, no iframes, no JSON, no rendering script. The only author script is jQuery, used for sticky-header positioning (Cloudflare injects its own beacon script; it is irrelevant to parsing). Plain `curl` returns the full table.
55-- **`robots.txt` is `Disallow:` (empty).** Scraping is permitted.
56-- **`If-Modified-Since` is honoured.** A request carrying the exact `last-modified` value returns `304` with an empty body; an older value returns `200`.
57-- **The header is five rows, not four.** Row 0 is the `Last update:` banner. Row 1 carries the table title, the as-of stamp, and one **date per event**. Row 2 carries the fixed column labels. Row 3 carries one **name per event**. Row 4 carries the per-event sub-column labels.
58-- **Fixed columns span ten grid columns, not eight.** `Rank`, `Name`, `YEAR of Birth`, `Club`, `Licence`, `Total Points` are one column each; `Domestic` and `International` are `colspan=2` each, and the two sub-columns under each are a **points subtotal and a count of events that contributed to it**.
59-- **Each event is two grid columns, not one.** Row 4 labels them `Rank` and `realPoint` — the fencer's **placing** at that event and the **points** it awarded. Row 3 gives the event name and row 1 gives its date at the same event index; zip them.
60-- **Domestic vs. international is published per event**, as a `class="domestic"` / `class="international"` attribute on the event-name cell. It is the source's own classification and must be carried through, not re-derived: the cadet table classes `U14 to Cadet Transition Bonus - 2026` as `international`, and the junior table classes `Cadet to Junior Transition Bonus - 2026` the same way. A rule Flunge invented would disagree with the source about the fencer's own published subtotals.
61-- **The event set differs per table** and must be read from each table's own header. The junior table lists FIE Junior World Cups and a Cadet-to-Junior transition bonus; the cadet table lists EFC Cadet events and a U14-to-Cadet transition bonus.
62-- **Dates are UK format** — `DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM` in the header banner, `DD Mon YY` per event column. Never parse as US.
63-- **Points are published as bare integers.** No cell in either table contains a decimal point. `37210` is what the source renders. See the [open question](#risks-and-open-questions) about whether that is a scaled value.
64-- **Ranks are shared, and the field is denser than the highest rank.** The cadet table's 58 rows run to rank 48 (ranks 42 and 48 are each shared by several fencers). **A chip's field size must be the parsed row count, never the highest rank.** The project brief's stated counts — 59 and 44 ranked fencers — are each one high, which is a small illustration of the same point: derive the number, do not carry it.
65-- **A bogus slug 404s; an unlisted-but-real slug returns 200 with a full table.** `definitely-not-a-real-table.html` returns a WordPress 404 page. `cadet-mens-sabre.html`, `junior-mens-sabre.html`, and `senior-mens-epee.html` all return `200` with a well-formed table. **Status codes therefore cannot be the integrity check** — structural validation is.
66-
67-### The counted set is reconstructible, and it reconciles
68-
69-The table publishes each fencer's `Domestic` and `International` subtotals together with **how many events contributed to each**. Taking the highest-scoring _n_ domestic events and the highest-scoring _m_ international events, where _n_ and _m_ are the published counts, reproduces both subtotals exactly — and `domestic + international == total` on every row.
70-
71-Measured across both tables:
72-
73-- **101 of 101 rows reconcile** under highest-scoring-_n_.
74-- The obvious competing hypothesis — that the counted events are simply the _most recent_ _n_ — reconciles on only **53 of 58** cadet rows and **37 of 43** junior rows, so it is ruled out rather than merely unchosen.
75-- On **5 rows** (4 selections in cadet, 1 in junior) the _n_-th and _(n+1)_-th event in a bucket are tied on points. The subtotal is unaffected, but _which_ event is the marginal counted one is then not determined by the published data. See [Boundary ties](#boundary-ties).
76-
77-This matters more than it looks. It means British can meet the **same reconcile-or-refuse contract** every other composition source in `view/standings/fencer.rs` already meets: emit a `complete` breakdown only when the counted entries sum to the card's published points within tolerance, and refuse rather than show a misleading partial list.
78-
79-Two things this evidence does **not** establish, and the design does not claim:
--
266:### Where the membership id lives
267-
268-A sidecar Cosmos document in `fencer_british_licences`, keyed by fencer id (`bfl-{fencerViewId}`), holding `{ fencerId, membershipId, setBy, setAt }`. Last write wins. Anyone who tracks the fencer may set or correct it. The membership id is still never serialized on standings or share responses.
269-
270-It must not live on `FencerFields`. That document is scraper-owned: `SyncFencerInfo` clones it, `merge_into`s FencingTracker profile fields, and `patch_document`s the result. A hand-typed value on that struct is one refresh away from being clobbered. The sidecar collection is a separate record the scraper is structurally unable to address; `fencer_refresh_merge_does_not_patch_a_licence_path` pins that.
271-
272-`GET /api/v2/user/me` still returns `trackedFencers[].britishFencingLicence` as a **hydrated** field so the settings editor does not need a new read endpoint. The user document is not the source of truth: writes go to the sidecar, and a one-shot migration strips leftover per-user values.
273-
274-The write is a **v3 route**, per the golden principle that new API work does not go in `v2/`:
275-
276-```
277-PUT /api/v3/user/tracked-fencers/{fencerId}/british-fencing-membership
278-Body: { "membershipId": "142013" }  |  { "membershipId": null }   // clears it
279-```
280-
281-hosted by a small `crate::v3::user::rest::router()` nested at `/user` in the protected v3 router. It validates that the caller tracks `fencerId`, trims the input, rejects anything that is not 1–32 characters, and stores `None` for an empty or null value, recording `setBy` / `setAt`.
282-
283-The alternative write path — the existing generic `PATCH /api/v2/user/me` json-patch that the frontend already calls — is deliberately not used. `validate_user_patch_paths` has an explicit kill switch (`user.patch_tracked_fencers_lockdown_enabled`) for exactly `/trackedFencers` paths, so building a new feature on that path means building on something the codebase already has a lever to disable.
284-
285-#### Decision reversal (2026-09-04)
286-
287-The original design stored the licence on `UserFields.tracked_fencers[]` as a private per-account assertion. It used "household" to mean "one user account". That conflation is what broke: two parents tracking the same child is the normal case, not an edge case, and they saw different British standings because only one account had typed the number.
288-
289-This objection is overruled: two accounts in one household tracking the same fencer is the normal case, and a licence only one of them can see is worse than a shared value one of them may have to correct. The scraper-ownership objection was **not** dismissed: the shared value lives in `fencer_british_licences`, not on `FencerFields`.
290-
291-Migration of existing per-user values: where exactly one distinct licence exists across all accounts tracking a fencer, adopt it (provenance = the lexicographically-smallest asserting user id). Where two or more accounts asserted different licences, leave the shared record unset, log a warning with the fencer id and the distinct-count (**never** the licence values), and let a human set it. After writing the sidecar, strip `britishFencingLicence` from user documents so there is one source of truth.
292-
293-Standings-history capture no longer has a multi-asserter ambiguity path. One shared record cannot produce two values; the previous `resolve_british_licence` / `BritishLicenceResolution::Ambiguous` machinery is gone.
294-
295-Share links stay owner-only. A share link is an anonymous grant resolved through the link owner's tracked-fencer list (the owner tracks the bound fencer by construction) and then the shared licence. The public unauthenticated `GET /standings/fencer/{id}` still does not load the shared licence. Broadening what a share link exposes beyond that owner-scoped grant is a separate decision.
296-
297-#### The consequence: British items need a tracking viewing context
298-
299-This is the part of the design most likely to surprise a reviewer, so it is stated plainly rather than buried.
300-
301-`GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{fencer_id}` is a **public** route. The licence is a shared fencer property, but loading it for every anonymous fencer-id request would publish British standings to the open internet. The endpoint therefore still needs a viewing context that tracks the fencer: the signed-in caller's own tracked-fencer list, or a live results-share link that already identifies both an owner and exactly one fencer.
302-
303-For the owner's Results page, **layer the existing `optional_auth_middleware` onto the standings router and, if the signed-in caller tracks this fencer, resolve the shared licence.** This is not a new mechanism. `view/registrations.rs` already defines that middleware for exactly this shape — "lets `/field-strength` stay reachable by signed-out visitors while still letting signed-in callers get their own account's `fencerMarkers`" — and its handler already takes `authed: Option<Extension<AuthenticatedUser>>`. The middleware moves to a shared location and gains a second consumer. Two accounts tracking the same fencer both see British standings after either one sets the licence.
304-
305-For a shared Results page, **the bearer link is the viewing context; Clerk auth is neither required nor consulted.** Add share-specific reads under the existing anonymous, no-store surface:
306-
307-```
308-GET /api/v3/share/results/view/standings
309-GET /api/v3/share/results/view/standings/{standingKey}/composition
310-Header: X-Flunge-Share-Token: {token}
311-```
312-
313-Both handlers resolve the live `ResultsShareLinkFields`, confirm the owner tracks the bound `fencer_id`, and pass the fencer's **shared** licence to the same internal standings/composition assembly used by the owner endpoints. The fencer id is deliberately absent from these route paths: a link cannot be used to ask about a different fencer. The membership id is likewise absent from the response; only the derived standing and composition cross the wire.
314-
315-These routes inherit the results-share contract rather than creating a second anonymous-auth mechanism: the token stays in `X-Flunge-Share-Token`, missing/unknown/revoked/expired/owner-gone links collapse to the existing generic 404, successful and failed responses are `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and the existing share-view rate limit applies. A recipient's Clerk session, if present, is ignored. Clearing or changing the shared membership id changes the link's next response immediately; disconnecting the fencer revokes the link under the existing share-link rule.
316-
317-What follows, all of it intended:
318-
319-- **An ordinary signed-out visitor sees no British chips.** National, Regional, and Unified chips are unchanged for them because a bare fencer id is not a tracking viewing context, even though a shared licence may exist.
320-- **A live shared results link shows British chips without sign-in**, resolved through the owner's tracking of the bound fencer plus the shared licence, and the chip's composition modal reads through the same bearer link. This is part of the link's one-fencer results grant, alongside the owner-scoped videos it already exposes. The grant is not widened to a public fencer-id read.
321-- **Two accounts tracking the same fencer share the licence.** Anyone who tracks the fencer may set or correct it; last write wins, with `setBy` / `setAt` provenance. Two parents in one household each have their own account, and that is the normal case — not an edge case to be papered over by duplicating the assertion.
322-- **`crate::recommendations::standings` sees no British items**, because it calls the fetch path with no user context. That matches the non-goal exactly, and it holds structurally rather than by a filter someone must remember to keep.
323-
324-### Not-yet-ranked
325-
326-A licence that matches no row on a table yields **no item for that table**, and nothing else. No error, no warning, no placeholder chip. Concretely:

                 "alias_rules.bzl": """"Alias that transitions its target to `compilation_mode=opt`.  Use `transition_alias="opt"` to enable."""

load("@rules_cc//cc:defs.bzl", "CcInfo")
load("@rules_rust//rust:rust_common.bzl", "COMMON_PROVIDERS")

def _transition_alias_impl(ctx):
    # `ctx.attr.actual` is a list of 1 item due to the transition
    providers = [ctx.attr.actual[0][provider] for provider in COMMON_PROVIDERS]
    if CcInfo in ctx.attr.actual[0]:
        providers.append(ctx.attr.actual[0][CcInfo])
    return providers

def _change_compilation_mode(compilation_mode):
    def _change_compilation_mode_impl(_settings, _attr):
        return {
            "//command_line_option:compilation_mode": compilation_mode,
        }

    return transition(
        implementation = _change_compilation_mode_impl,
        inputs = [],
        outputs = [
            "//command_line_option:compilation_mode",
        ],
    )

def _transition_alias_rule(compilation_mode):
    return rule(
        implementation = _transition_alias_impl,
        provides = COMMON_PROVIDERS,
        attrs = {
            "actual": attr.label(
                mandatory = True,
                doc = "`rust_library()` target to transition to `compilation_mode=opt`.",
                providers = COMMON_PROVIDERS,
                cfg = _change_compilation_mode(compilation_mode),
            ),
            "_allowlist_function_transition": attr.label(
                default = "@bazel_tools//tools/allowlists/function_transition_allowlist",
            ),
        },
        doc = "Transitions a Rust library crate to the `compilation_mode=opt`.",
    )

transition_alias_dbg = _transition_alias_rule("dbg")
transition_alias_fastbuild = _transition_alias_rule("fastbuild")
transition_alias_opt = _transition_alias_rule("opt")

# An identifier that represent common dependencies (unconditional).
_COMMON_CONDITION = ""

def _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps):
    """Flatten a list of dependency maps into one dictionary.

    Dependency maps have the following structure:

    ```python
    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {
        # The first key in the map is a Bazel package
        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.
        "workspace_member_package": {

            # Not all dependencies are supported for all platforms.
            # the condition key is the condition required to be true
            # on the host platform.
            "condition": {

                # An alias to a crate target.     # The label of the crate target the
                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.
                "package_name":                   "@full//:label",
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))
                    continue

                # Alert on any miss-matched dependencies
                inconsistent_entries = []
                for crate_name, crate_label in deps_map.items():
                    existing = dependencies[pkg_name][condition].get(crate_name)
                    if existing and existing != crate_label:
                        inconsistent_entries.append((crate_name, existing, crate_label))
                    dependencies[pkg_name][condition].update({crate_name: crate_label})

    return dependencies

def crate_deps(deps, package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of the requested crates for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        deps (list): The desired list of crate targets.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()`.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if not deps:
        return []

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Join both sets of dependencies
    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps([
        _NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES,
        _NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
    ]).pop(package_name, {})

    # Combine all conditional packages so we can easily index over a flat list
    # TODO: Perhaps this should actually return select statements and maintain
    # the conditionals of the dependencies
    flat_deps = {}
    for deps_set in dependencies.values():
        for crate_name, crate_label in deps_set.items():
            flat_deps.update({crate_name: crate_label})

    missing_crates = []
    crate_targets = []
    for crate_target in deps:
        if crate_target not in flat_deps:
            missing_crates.append(crate_target)
        else:
            crate_targets.append(flat_deps[crate_target])

        fail("Could not find crates `{}` among dependencies of `{}`. Available dependencies were `{}`".format(
            missing_crates,
            package_name,
            dependencies,

    return crate_targets

def all_crate_deps(
        normal = False, 
        normal_dev = False, 
        proc_macro = False, 
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of all requested direct crate dependencies \
    for the package where this macro is called.

    If no parameters are set, all normal dependencies are returned. Setting any one flag will
    otherwise impact the contents of the returned list.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_dependency_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

    # Default to always using normal dependencies
    if not all_dependency_maps:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)

    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not dependencies:
        if dependencies == None:
            fail("Tried to get all_crate_deps for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")
        else:
            return []

    crate_deps = list(dependencies.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).values())
    for condition, deps in dependencies.items():
        crate_deps += selects.with_or({
            tuple(_CONDITIONS[condition]): deps.values(),
            "//conditions:default": [],
        })

    return crate_deps

def aliases(
        normal = False,
        normal_dev = False,
        proc_macro = False,
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Produces a map of Crate alias names to their original label

    If no dependency kinds are specified, `normal` and `proc_macro` are used by default.
    Setting any one flag will otherwise determine the contents of the returned dict.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        dict: The aliases of all associated packages
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_aliases_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    # Default to always using normal aliases
    if not all_aliases_maps:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    aliases = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_aliases_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not aliases:
        return dict()

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:
        return dict(common_items)

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.
    crate_aliases = {"//conditions:default": dict(common_items)}
    for condition, deps in aliases.items():
        condition_triples = _CONDITIONS[condition]
        for triple in condition_triples:
            if triple in crate_aliases:
                crate_aliases[triple].update(deps)
            else:
                crate_aliases.update({triple: dict(deps.items() + common_items)})

    return select(crate_aliases)

# An identifier that represent common dependencies (unconditional).
_COMMON_CONDITION = ""

def _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps):
    """Flatten a list of dependency maps into one dictionary.

    Dependency maps have the following structure:

    ```python
    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {
        # The first key in the map is a Bazel package
        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.
        "workspace_member_package": {

            # Not all dependencies are supported for all platforms.
            # the condition key is the condition required to be true
            # on the host platform.
            "condition": {

                # An alias to a crate target.     # The label of the crate target the
                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.
                "package_name":                   "@full//:label",
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))
                    continue

                # Alert on any miss-matched dependencies
                inconsistent_entries = []
                for crate_name, crate_label in deps_map.items():
                    existing = dependencies[pkg_name][condition].get(crate_name)
                    if existing and existing != crate_label:
                        inconsistent_entries.append((crate_name, existing, crate_label))
                    dependencies[pkg_name][condition].update({crate_name: crate_label})

    return dependencies

def crate_deps(deps, package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of the requested crates for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        deps (list): The desired list of crate targets.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()`.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if not deps:
        return []

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Join both sets of dependencies
    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps([
        _NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES,
        _NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,

    # the conditionals of the dependencies

    crate_targets = []

def all_crate_deps(
        normal = False, 
        normal_dev = False, 
        proc_macro = False, 
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of all requested direct crate dependencies \
    for the package where this macro is called.

    If no parameters are set, all normal dependencies are returned. Setting any one flag will
    otherwise impact the contents of the returned list.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_dependency_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

    # Default to always using normal dependencies
    if not all_dependency_maps:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)

    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not dependencies:
        if dependencies == None:
            fail("Tried to get all_crate_deps for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")
        else:
            return []

    crate_deps = list(dependencies.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).values())
    for condition, deps in dependencies.items():
        crate_deps += selects.with_or({
            tuple(_CONDITIONS[condition]): deps.values(),
            "//conditions:default": [],
        })

    return crate_deps

def aliases(

        normal_dev = False,
        proc_macro = False,
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):

    If no dependency kinds are specified, `normal` and `proc_macro` are used by default.
    Setting any one flag will otherwise determine the contents of the returned dict.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        dict: The aliases of all associated packages
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_aliases_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    # Default to always using normal aliases
    if not all_aliases_maps:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    aliases = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_aliases_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not aliases:
        return dict()

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:
        return dict(common_items)

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.
    crate_aliases = {"//conditions:default": dict(common_items)}
    for condition, deps in aliases.items():
        condition_triples = _CONDITIONS[condition]

            if triple in crate_aliases:
                crate_aliases[triple].update(deps)
            else:
                crate_aliases.update({triple: dict(deps.items() + common_items)})

    return select(crate_aliases)

A publish therefore costs exactly its source sweep: ~137 s clean, ~1,487 s if every list exhausts the realignment pool, both inside the 1,800 s task budget. Previously this path resolved ~11,000 rows against FencingTracker inline at 55-65/minute — about three hours — and could not complete: it either died at the task timeout having published nothing, or terminated only because an egress cooldown fast-failed the backlog and published a snapshot missing most of its identities.  - `sweep_unified_identities` is the identity half, on its own 15-minute cadence (`unified.identity_sweep_cadence_minutes`); `POST /api/v2/admin/tasks/sweep_unified_identities/exec` runs one slice immediately. It never continues past a paused guard: a paused guard rejects every request in under a millisecond, so continuing would march the whole working set past the retry horizon without asking a single question, which is exactly how the old inline sweep "completed". Bindings and attempts flush in batches, so an interrupted run keeps the lookups it already paid for and the next run continues rather than restarting. Resolved bindings live at `view:standings:unified:identity:v1:bindings`, versioned independently of `UNIFIED_CATALOG_CACHE_VERSION` precisely so a payload-shape bump cannot discard hours of third-party resolution. A cold ~11,000-row catalog converges in roughly seven hours. The whole run executes under `egress::as_background`, and `fencingtracker.background_max_requests_per_hour` is now a real ceiling (6,000/hour ≈ a sixth of what the 10 req/s limiter permits) rather than 0/disabled, so identity resolution can never starve user-facing lookups.

Both halves are needed to judge Unified health: a successful publish no longer implies complete data, which is why the Admin card renders coverage next to the refresh result rather than only a green chip.
-- `snapshot_standings_history` is the twice-weekly standings-history capture (`0 30 7 * * Mon,Thu` UTC, up to 30 minutes of per-replica jitter). It walks `get_all_connected_fencer_ids()` in sorted order and reads `get_fencer_standings`, passing each fencer's British Fencing licence when `crate::v2::user::get_all_connected_fencer_licences()` resolves exactly one distinct licence for them across every household; when two or more households assert _different_ licences for the same fencer, capture refuses British for that fencer (`capture::resolve_british_licence`), logs a `warn` naming the fencer id and the distinct-licence count (never the licence values), and tallies it in `CaptureCounts.britishLicenceAmbiguous` — USA scopes for that fencer are captured either way. It stores one Cosmos snapshot per standing plus a per-fencer receipt, and writes the card's movement summary to Redis hash `standings:history:v1:movement`. Youth-national and per-region regional compositions are live USA Fencing fetches gated on `standings_history.capture_live_compositions` (default off) and the shared `standings:refresh:cooldown_until` cooldown; National CJS, Unified, and British counted sets are captured either way (British composition is not a live fetch). If `standings.british_rankings_enabled` is off at the start of a run, the run logs that loudly and records it as `CaptureCounts.britishRankingsFlagDisabled`, since a disabled flag otherwise degrades every British standing to a silent `standingAbsent` gap indistinguishable from "not ranked". `POST /api/v2/admin/tasks/snapshot_standings_history/exec` is the manual path (Admin Tasks **Run Now**); optional `?runId=YYYY-MM-DD` re-runs a past Monday/Thursday slot (400 if the date is not a slot or is later than the most recent one). A replica that loses the cluster-wide `SET NX` lock at `standings:history:v1:snapshot-lock` returns `already_running`, not a failure. Scheduled ticks no-op while `standings_history.enabled` is false; a manual Run Now still captures. Startup requests a catch-up run when the most recent slot has no run record. Partial success (any failed receipt or unattempted fencer) is an `Err` with counts, while every document that did succeed remains written. `GET /api/v2/admin/standings-history` (`ops`) returns the persisted run-state (`lastAttemptAt`, `lastAttemptRunId`, `lastSuccessAt`, `lastFailureAt`, `lastFailureReason`, `lastRunCounts`, `oldestSnapshotAt`, `newestSnapshotAt`), including the British counters on `lastRunCounts`, so a process restart does not hide the last outcome. Intended caller: Admin Tasks / ops. A known limitation: an ambiguous fencer's British graph reads as `standingAbsent` ("not ranked that day") rather than "uncaptured", since `fencer_history.rs`'s gap classifier has no `ambiguous` gap kind and adding one would widen the wire contract on both clients — recorded, not fixed, here. See [Standings trajectory over time](../design-docs/standings-trajectory-over-time.md).
+- `snapshot_standings_history` is the twice-weekly standings-history capture (`0 30 7 * * Mon,Thu` UTC, up to 30 minutes of per-replica jitter). It walks `get_all_connected_fencer_ids()` in sorted order and reads `get_fencer_standings`, passing each fencer's shared British Fencing licence from `get_all_connected_fencer_ids_and_licences()` when one is set. The licence is a property of the fencer, not a per-account assertion, so capture cannot observe two values for the same fencer. It stores one Cosmos snapshot per standing plus a per-fencer receipt, and writes the card's movement summary to Redis hash `standings:history:v1:movement`. Youth-national and per-region regional compositions are live USA Fencing fetches gated on `standings_history.capture_live_compositions` (default off) and the shared `standings:refresh:cooldown_until` cooldown; National CJS, Unified, and British counted sets are captured either way (British composition is not a live fetch). A replica that loses the cluster-wide `SET NX` lock at `standings:history:v1:snapshot-lock` returns `already_running`, not a failure. Scheduled ticks no-op while `standings_history.enabled` is false; a manual Run Now still captures. Startup requests a catch-up run when the most recent slot has no run record. Partial success (any failed receipt or unattempted fencer) is an `Err` with counts, while every document that did succeed remains written. `GET /api/v2/admin/standings-history` (`ops`) returns the persisted run-state (`lastAttemptAt`, `lastAttemptRunId`, `lastSuccessAt`, `lastFailureAt`, `lastFailureReason`, `lastRunCounts`, `oldestSnapshotAt`, `newestSnapshotAt`), including the British counters on `lastRunCounts`, so a process restart does not hide the last outcome. Intended caller: Admin Tasks / ops. See [Standings trajectory over time](../design-docs/standings-trajectory-over-time.md).
 - **Standings population policy reworked to be aggressive (2026-07-15).** The `max_jobs_per_run=1` default (full 204-job sweep in ~2 days) was a holdover from an older, more blocking-prone standings implementation and was never revisited after `#562` introduced the current stalest-first incremental design — it left nearly every regional list cold for days after the `:v2` cache-key bump below (`#863`), since the recommendation-serving path is cache-only and never self-heals from request traffic. `max_jobs_per_run` is now `16` (see `[standings]` in `backend/config-common.toml` for the full rationale), giving a full sweep in ~3.2 hours instead of ~2 days. This is a real concurrency increase on the always-on path, not merely a frequency change: `fetch_concurrency = FETCH_CONCURRENCY.min(selected_jobs.len())` in `randomized_refresh.rs` means effective job concurrency rises from 1 (the old default) to 8, and since each job's `enrich_standings_with_ids` opens its own 7-wide semaphore, peak concurrent upstream fencingtracker requests rises from ~7 to ~56. This was not (and could not safely be) load-tested against production USA Fencing from this change alone; the existing `redis_backoff` error-streak/cooldown mechanism in `standings_index::randomized_refresh` (shrinks the effective per-run budget on failures, then pauses entirely on a 403 or high failure rate) remains the live governor. If upstream blocking is observed at this rate, record the observed threshold here and in `config-common.toml`, and lower `max_jobs_per_run` to the last-known-safe value.
 - **Cache-key version bumps now self-heal on process startup instead of waiting on the incremental tick.** `backend/admintasks/src/rebuild_standings_index.rs::heal_view_cache_version_bump_on_startup` compares `view::standings::STANDINGS_VIEW_CACHE_VERSION` against the value last seen (stored at Redis key `standings:view_cache:version_seen`) and, on a change (including the first deploy of this mechanism), requests one full `rebuild_standings_index` sweep. A fleet of replicas racing this at boot is coordinated by a short-TTL `SET NX` lock (`standings:view_cache:version_heal_lock`) rather than the version key itself, so a replica that loses the race just skips _requesting_ a sweep this boot — it never marks the bump as healed. The sweep is routed through `force_full_refresh` + `TaskManager::try_spawn_now("rebuild_standings_index")` rather than called directly, so it runs as a normal task execution: `TaskManager`'s scheduler defers the 15-min cron tick while a sweep is already running (rather than racing it for the shared `standings:index` Redis state), and `standings:view_cache:version_seen` is only written once that sweep actually returns `Ok` — a sweep that errors partway through (an upstream 403, a Redis blip, the pod getting rescheduled) leaves the marker unset so the next boot retries, instead of being silently marked healed and never retried. `run_full_refresh` also now records a per-job last-refreshed timestamp for every job it sweeps (previously only the incremental path did), so the very next incremental tick after a heal doesn't immediately treat all ~204 jobs as never-refreshed and re-fetch the whole catalog again. Gated on `CONF.background_tasks.enabled` (same flag `TaskManager::start` uses), so tests/local dev never touch Redis or upstream for this. Bumping `STANDINGS_VIEW_CACHE_VERSION` in step with the `NATIONAL_STANDINGS_VIEW_CACHE_KEY`/`REGIONAL_STANDINGS_VIEW_CACHE_KEY` literals below (a unit test in `view/standings/mod.rs` guards against forgetting) is now the only step needed for a future key bump to heal promptly, instead of requiring an operator to click "Run + Refresh List" manually.
 - **`regional_entry_id` never survived this cache's serde_json round-trip (2026-07-15 fix, no wire contract change).** `usafencing::model::FencerStanding::regional_entry_id` (the regional whole-list scrape's internal per-row id, needed to call the per-fencer regional breakdown endpoint) had shipped `#[serde(skip)]`, which — since this Redis hash is the _only_ channel from the scraper to the recommendations serving path — silently discarded it on every single write, so every cached regional standing came back `regional_entry_id: None` regardless of what the scraper produced. This made every regional (RYC/RJCC/ROC) projected-impact evidence evaluation refuse for lack of a replacement basis, in every environment, since the field was introduced (#810) — this was the third investigation of that user-visible symptom (#827, #853, #857) before staging logs and live cache contents pinned the actual cause. Fixed by removing the `skip` attribute so the field round-trips normally, and adding a `FencerStandingPublic` REST DTO (dropping just that one field) for the two routes above and `usafencing::api::rest`'s `/standings/national/{classifier}` and `/standings/region/{region_id}/{classifier}`, which previously serialized `FencerStanding` directly — since the field was never actually emitted before either (the `skip` stripped it from responses too), every route's JSON response shape is byte-for-byte unchanged. The cache key literals gained a `:v2` suffix (`view:standings:national:v2`/`view:standings:regional:v2`, the same "bump the namespace" convention `docs/backend/recommendations.md`'s `recommendations_compute_v2` rename uses) so entries written under the old key — permanently missing the field, with no TTL to expire them out on its own — are orphaned rather than served stale; `get_standings`'s existing on-miss `refresh_standings_cache` repopulates each region/classifier under the new key on its next read or `rebuild_standings_index` tick. See `docs/backend/recommendations.md`'s matching note for the paired sec-17 "known zero vs. unknown" refusal-semantics fix in the projected-impact contributor that consumes this cache.

/bin/zsh -lc '"$BOSS_BIN" propose review-guide --body '"'# Shared British Fencing licences across tracking accounts

## Orientation

Two parents following the same child could see different British standings: only the account that entered the membership number could see them. This change makes one entry available to everyone tracking that fencer, so either parent can supply or correct it. A licence is the British Fencing membership number used to find the fencer in published rankings; tracking means adding that fencer to an account’s connected-fencer list.

The change lives in the backend services serving settings, rankings, and shared results. The latest saved licence becomes the shared value, including when someone clears it. Viewing British standings still requires a signed-in account that tracks the fencer, or a live results-share link whose owner tracks that fencer. A results-share link grants access to results for one particular fencer without requiring the recipient to sign in.

The existing British rankings feature brings published rankings and their points breakdowns onto the Results page alongside USA Fencing standings. This PR changes the account-specific membership-number connection underneath that feature, reusing its existing editor and ranking displays. The [design’s decision reversal](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/docs/design-docs/british-fencing-rankings-as-a-standings-source.md#L266-L303) explains the two-parent case and why shared storage remains separate from automatically refreshed fencer profiles.

## Change overview

This corrects the inconsistent experience across accounts by changing licence ownership from an account annotation to a fencer property. Any tracker can set, replace, or clear the value; the record stores who last wrote it and when. Sharing the value does not make British standings public to everyone who knows a fencer identifier.

Existing account values move through an explicit migration: agreement produces a shared licence, while disagreement preserves the old assertions for human reconciliation. Background standings-history capture then consumes one shared value per fencer instead of resolving competing account assertions.

## Core implementation

A new "'`fencer_licence` Rust package owns the record model, database operations, and migration planner. Its database collection is supplied by the caller, keeping it independent of `blob`, the backend application package. `blob` connects that package to writes, profile responses, standings reads, and the migration task. See the [package boundary](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/lib.rs#L1-L18).

The licence lives in a **sidecar**, meaning a separate database record associated with the fencer, in the Cosmos document database collection `fencer_british_licences`. Settings keep the existing response field through **hydration**: filling the response from shared storage immediately before returning it.

## Implementation walkthrough

### 1. Save one record per fencer through the existing editor

The existing `PUT /api/v3/user/tracked-fencers/{fencerId}/british-fencing-membership` route still checks that the authenticated account tracks the fencer. It trims input, accepts up to 32 characters, treats null or whitespace-only input as clearing, and returns 204 after success. These are [existing route semantics](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v3/user.rs#L51-L109), rather than new membership verification.

The decisive write change is in [the user helper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L249-L275): after checking tracking again, it calls `set_licence` instead of patching the user document. The [application wrapper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/fencer_licence.rs#L30-L43) supplies the writer and current time.

The [stored model](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/model.rs#L9-L17) is small:

```rust
pub struct FencerLicenceFields {
  pub fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
  #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  pub membership_id: Option<String>,
  pub set_by: TypedId<UserId>,
  pub set_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```

`setBy` and `setAt` identify the latest writer and write time. The [repository](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/repository.rs#L15-L28) derives the key `bfl-{fencerId}`. Its [upsert](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/repository.rs#L79-L94)—create or replace at that key—implements last-write-wins behavior. Clearing keeps a record with no membership number and the latest provenance.

This storage boundary matters because the existing [profile refresh](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/fencingtracker/mod.rs#L438-L486) merges imported profile data and patches `DB.fencers`. It does not write the licence collection, and saving a licence does not require a corresponding profile document.

### 2. Preserve the settings response while changing its source

[Both GET `/user/me` and the generic profile PATCH response](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/app.rs#L808-L834) now hydrate licences. The [repository batches tracked fencer identifiers into one filtered query](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/repository.rs#L43-L77), avoiding a lookup per fencer. An empty tracked list needs no query.

[Hydration overwrites every response value](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/fencer_licence.rs#L69-L91), including old account-local values:

```rust
for tracked in &mut user.fields.tracked_fencers {
  tracked.british_fencing_licence = by_fencer.get(&tracked.fencer_id).cloned().flatten();
}
```

A shared-storage read error becomes an empty map, so the profile still returns with those fields unset. The [existing settings input](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/frontend/src/SettingsPage.tsx#L455-L464) can continue reading `britishFencingLicence`, calling the dedicated write route, and refreshing the account response.

The [generic JSON patch validator](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L470-L512) additionally rejects operation paths containing `britishFencingLicence`, independent of the setting that blocks changes to tracked fencers. ### 3. Resolve shared data only after checking viewing permission

The [new resolver](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs#L748-L787) separates the tracking check from fetching the number:

```rust
if !may_resolve_british_licence(tracked, fencer_id) {
  return None;
}
```

The tracking check uses the [existing exact fencer-identifier comparison](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/share/mod.rs#L43-L50).

[Shared standings](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/share/view.rs#L256-L290) and [shared composition](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/share/view.rs#L301-L343) instead supply the live link owner’s tracking list and the fencer bound to that link. ### Worked example: one parent enters the number

Illustrative input: Alice and Bob both track `f.u.100344622`; neither initially has a licence. Alice submits `{"membershipId":" 142013 "}`. Assume British rankings are enabled and a published table contains that licence.

1. **Before:** the [old write helper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/9806138106ee6c5da6840b58b468bbc4f3e0b8af/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L246-L268) stored the trimmed number only in Alice’s user document. The [old standings resolver](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/9806138106ee6c5da6840b58b468bbc4f3e0b8af/backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs#L756-L764) read the requesting account’s field. Bob’s value remained absent, so his response omitted British standings.
2. **Now:** the same [route normalization](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v3/user.rs#L65-L108) yields `142013`, and the shared write stores it at `bfl-f.u.100344622`, attributed to Alice. On Bob’s next profile read, hydration supplies that number. On his next standings read, tracking passes the gate even though he entered nothing, and the resolver loads the same record.
3. **Visible result:** both accounts can receive the British ranking item for that licence. The [unchanged ranking assembly](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs#L834-L911) appends British items only when a licence is supplied, the runtime switch enables British rankings, and matching published data is available.

If Bob subsequently clears the field, the shared record becomes cleared for both accounts. An ordinary signed-out request still passes no licence to assembly, even while the shared record contains a number; sharing storage does not bypass the viewing gate.

### 4. Migrate old assertions, then simplify history capture

The [pure migration planner](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/migrate.rs#L66-L111) groups account assertions by fencer and distinct licence. One distinct number produces an adoption decision, with the alphabetically first asserting user identifier selected as provenance. Multiple distinct numbers produce a conflict containing only the fencer identifier and distinct count.

The [migration orchestration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/fencer_licence.rs#L149-L220) scans users and existing shared records, skips adoption for identifiers already found in shared storage, and writes the other agreed values. Conflict decisions create no shared value; their warnings contain the fencer identifier and count. Conflicted fencers remain in a preservation set, so their old account values survive cleanup. Other old values are removed by patching the affected user documents and invalidating their cached copies.

The operation is exposed as the [explicit admin task `migrate_british_fencing_licences`](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/admintasks/src/migrate_british_fencing_licences.rs#L10-L31). [Startup deliberately does not run it](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/app.rs#L85-L90), avoiding repeated full user scans on every backend process start.

For history capture, [enumeration now combines connected USA Fencing identifiers with shared licence records](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L816-L834), excluding unconnected fencers and cleared values. [Capture builds a direct identifier-to-licence map](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/standings_history/capture.rs#L63-L115). The old disagreement resolver and `britishLicenceAmbiguous` diagnostic disappear; conflict handling now belongs to migration of historical assertions.

This change makes one entry available to everyone tracking that fencer, so either parent can supply or correct it. ## Orientation

Two parents following the same child could see different British standings: only the account that entered the membership number could see them. This change makes one entry available to everyone tracking that fencer, so either parent can supply or correct it. A licence is the British Fencing membership number used to find the fencer in published rankings; tracking means adding that fencer to an account’s connected-fencer list.

The change lives in the backend services serving settings, rankings, and shared results. The latest saved licence becomes the shared value, including when someone clears it. Viewing British standings still requires a signed-in account that tracks the fencer, or a live results-share link whose owner tracks that fencer. A results-share link grants access to results for one particular fencer without requiring the recipient to sign in.

The existing British rankings feature brings published rankings and their points breakdowns onto the Results page alongside USA Fencing standings. This PR changes the account-specific membership-number connection underneath that feature, reusing its existing editor and ranking displays. The [design’s decision reversal](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/docs/design-docs/british-fencing-rankings-as-a-standings-source.md#L266-L303) explains the two-parent case and why shared storage remains separate from automatically refreshed fencer profiles.

## Change overview

This corrects the inconsistent experience across accounts by changing licence ownership from an account annotation to a fencer property. Any tracker can set, replace, or clear the value; the record stores who last wrote it and when. Sharing the value does not make British standings public to everyone who knows a fencer identifier.

Existing account values move through an explicit migration: agreement produces a shared licence, while disagreement preserves the old assertions for human reconciliation. Background standings-history capture then consumes one shared value per fencer instead of resolving competing account assertions.

## Core implementation

A new "'`fencer_licence` Rust package owns the record model, database operations, and migration planner. Its database collection is supplied by the caller, keeping it independent of `blob`, the backend application package. `blob` connects that package to writes, profile responses, standings reads, and the migration task. See the [package boundary](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/lib.rs#L1-L18).

The licence lives in a **sidecar**, meaning a separate database record associated with the fencer, in the Cosmos document database collection `fencer_british_licences`. Settings keep the existing response field through **hydration**: filling the response from shared storage immediately before returning it.

## Implementation walkthrough

### 1. Save one record per fencer through the existing editor

The existing `PUT /api/v3/user/tracked-fencers/{fencerId}/british-fencing-membership` route still checks that the authenticated account tracks the fencer. It trims input, accepts up to 32 characters, treats null or whitespace-only input as clearing, and returns 204 after success. These are [existing route semantics](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v3/user.rs#L51-L109), rather than new membership verification.

The decisive write change is in [the user helper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L249-L275): after checking tracking again, it calls `set_licence` instead of patching the user document. The [application wrapper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/fencer_licence.rs#L30-L43) supplies the writer and current time.

The [stored model](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/model.rs#L9-L17) is small:

```rust
pub struct FencerLicenceFields {
  pub fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
  #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  pub membership_id: Option<String>,
  pub set_by: TypedId<UserId>,
  pub set_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```

`setBy` and `setAt` identify the latest writer and write time. The [repository](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/fencer_licence/src/repository.rs#L15-L28) derives the key `bfl-{fencerId}`. ```rust
for tracked in &mut user.fields.tracked_fencers {
  tracked.british_fencing_licence = by_fencer.get(&tracked.fencer_id).cloned().flatten();
}
```

A shared-storage read error becomes an empty map, so the profile still returns with those fields unset. The [generic JSON patch validator](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L470-L512) additionally rejects operation paths containing `britishFencingLicence`, independent of the setting that blocks changes to tracked fencers. ```rust
if !may_resolve_british_licence(tracked, fencer_id) {
  return None;
}
```

Only after that check does it load the shared record. Missing, cleared, and failed reads all produce no licence. The tracking check uses the [existing exact fencer-identifier comparison](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/share/mod.rs#L43-L50).

The [history handler](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer_history.rs#L133-L151) does the same before finding the requested current standing.

[Shared standings](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/share/view.rs#L256-L290) and [shared composition](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/share/view.rs#L301-L343) instead supply the live link owner’s tracking list and the fencer bound to that link. A number entered by another tracker therefore works on the owner’s share page without changing which fencer the link grants access to.

Illustrative input: Alice and Bob both track `f.u.100344622`; neither initially has a licence. Alice submits `{"membershipId":" 142013 "}`. Assume British rankings are enabled and a published table contains that licence.

1. **Before:** the [old write helper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/9806138106ee6c5da6840b58b468bbc4f3e0b8af/backend/blob/src/v2/user.rs#L246-L268) stored the trimmed number only in Alice’s user document. The [old standings resolver](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/9806138106ee6c5da6840b58b468bbc4f3e0b8af/backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs#L756-L764) read the requesting account’s field. Bob’s value remained absent, so his response omitted British standings.
2. **Now:** the same [route normalization](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/v3/user.rs#L65-L108) yields `142013`, and the shared write stores it at `bfl-f.u.100344622`, attributed to Alice. On Bob’s next profile read, hydration supplies that number. On his next standings read, tracking passes the gate even though he entered nothing, and the resolver loads the same record.

The [unchanged ranking assembly](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/256630b62986cc513c42e7e9075e57011707ce9a/backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs#L834-L911) appends British items only when a licence is supplied, the runtime switch enables British rankings, and matching published data is available.

The change lives in the backend services serving settings, rankings, and shared results. The latest saved licence becomes the shared value, including when someone clears it. Viewing British standings still requires a signed-in account that tracks the fencer, or a live results-share link whose owner tracks that fencer. A results-share link grants access to results for one particular fencer without requiring the recipient to sign in.

The existing British rankings feature brings published rankings and their points breakdowns onto the Results page alongside USA Fencing standings. This PR changes the account-specific membership-number connection underneath that feature, reusing its existing editor and ranking displays. This corrects the inconsistent experience across accounts by changing licence ownership from an account annotation to a fencer property. Any tracker can set, replace, or clear the value; the record stores who last wrote it and when. Sharing the value does not make British standings public to everyone who knows a fencer identifier.
